To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a mutation in the ELMOD3 gene causes deafness in humans and that ELMOD3 regulates the actin cyto-skeleton and the Arl2 protein in the inner ear.
a mutation in a GTPase-activating protein (ELMOD3) is associated with hearing loss in humans, and that ELMOD3 interacts with Arl2 G-protein and regulates actin cytoskeletal structures.
we have identified a transition mutation in ELMOD2, an Arl-2 GTPase Activating Protein, which is associated with hearing impairment in humans.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the gene underlying DFNB88, a locus that was previously associated with hearing loss.
the identification of a new gene, ELMOD, that is associated with deafness in humans, and with the characterization of ELMOD in the inner ear and other epithelial cell types.
the identification of a mutation in ELMOD2 that is associated with a form of nonsyndromal hearing impairment and the characterization of ELMOD2 as an Arl2 GAP protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ELMOD3 gene, which encodes an Arl2-GAP, is associated with nonsydromic hearing impairment in humans.
the p.Leu 265Ser mutation in ELMOD is the cause for DFNB88 hearing loss.
this work provides the first evidence that ELMOD3 plays a role in the actin cyto-skeleton and that the p.Leu255Ser mutation in ELMOD 3 impairs its ability to bind to Arl2 G protein and actin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ELMOD3 has an essential role in hearing and that its mutation causes deafness.
we identified the first mutation in the ELMOD3 gene that is associated with human disease.
ELMOD3 has a novel function as a GTPase-activating protein for the small G protein Arl2, which is required for hearing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the p.Leu255Ser mutation in the ELMOD3 gene causes nonsyndromal, autosomal-recessive, prelingual deafness in the affected individuals of the PKDF468 family.
the ELMOD3 mutation identified here is associated with hearing loss in humans and that ELMOD3 functions as a GTPase-activating protein for Arl2.
ELMOD3 functions as an Arl2 GAP and is a novel regulator of the Arl2/ELMOD3/actin network in the inner ear.
